text: If a man marries a woman and then finds her displeasing because he has discovered something offensive about her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house.
And if, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man's wife,
and this second husband also turns against her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house—or if the second husband dies—

then her first husband, who divorced her, may not take her back as his wife, since she has been defiled. That would be detestable in the LORD's sight. You must not bring sin upon the land the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance.
When a man has just married, he is not to go out with the army or be assigned any other duty. He shall be free to stay at home for one year, to bring joy to the wife he has married.
No one is to take a pair of millstones—or even the upper stone—as security for a debt, for that would be taking a life as security.
If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers, an Israelite, and treats him as a slave and sells him, that kidnapper must die. You are to purge the evil from among you.

versions.text: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers, an Israelite, and treats him as a slave or sells him, that kidnapper must die. You are to purge the evil from among you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses a simple connective ("and sells him"), describing a single sequence of actions: seizing, enslaving, and selling. "Or" turns them into alternatives and subtly changes the legal condition.

text: In cases of skin disease, be careful to do exactly as the Levitical priests instruct you. Take care to follow what I have commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam along the way after you came out of Egypt.
When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, do not go into his house to collect what he offers as security.
Stay outside, and let the man to whom you are making the loan bring the pledge out to you.
If he is poor, do not go to sleep holding his pledge.
Be sure to return the pledge to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you. This will be counted as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.

versions.text: Return his cloak to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in it and bless you. This will be counted as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew distinguishes the "pledge" from "his garment"; keeping both terms preserves the link with verses 10-12 and reflects the emphatic infinitive ("be sure to return").

text: Do not exploit a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or a foreigner living in one of your towns.
Pay him his wages the same day, before the sun goes down, because he is poor and his life depends on it. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.

versions.text: Pay him his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and is counting on them. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
versions.explanation: "Each day before sunset" flattens two distinct clauses and reads awkwardly; also, "is counting on them" weakens the Hebrew idiom "he sets his life upon it," which conveys urgent dependence for survival.

text: Fathers are not to be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.
Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the orphan, and do not take a widow's garment as security.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you are harvesting in your field and overlook a sheaf, do not go back for it. Leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches again. What is left is for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
When you harvest the grapes in your vineyard, do not go back over the vines. What is left is for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
